positions.as_written: Treat the ground reaction force as a vector with a point of application, not as a number.
Use a walking aid to reduce limb load when the aim is mechanical rather than only balance.
Consider foot progression angle and stance width, since they change the knee moment without changing the force.
Read an insole or accelerometer figure as a proxy rather than as a ground reaction force.
Treat the ground reaction force as the input that alignment surgery works on.
Plan an osteotomy by where the force line should fall rather than by a target angle alone.
Expect a lateral wedge or a gait modification to produce a small mechanical change, and describe it as such.
Treat static alignment as a proxy for the dynamic moment, since they correlate imperfectly.
